typical_situation: Lead is already running the property as a short-let, either self-managed or through another management company (e.g. Pass the Keys, Hello Guest, MyProperty Host, Residential Estates), and is dissatisfied with underperformance — low reviews, poor occupancy vs the local market, operational failures like missed check-ins or unresolved maintenance, or a fee increase at renewal.
typical_motivation: Fix chronic underperformance or reduce management fees so the property finally hits the net income originally expected from short-letting, without having to become hands-on themselves.
typical_timeline: Gated by the notice period owed to the current management company (often weeks to a few months), sometimes deliberately timed to a natural quiet season for a clean handover of an established, review-rich listing.
what_meeting_should_lead_with: Skip re-pitching short-letting as a concept — this lead already believes in it. Lead instead with a specific, evidenced diagnosis of why the current setup underperforms (reviews, pricing, listing structure, communication) and only then contrast Stayful's model point-by-point against the current company, backed with real numbers and concrete proof points.

top_questions.question: How does Stayful's fee and service actually compare to my current management company?
top_questions.best_answer: Give a direct side-by-side: fee percentage, number of listing platforms, communication model (e.g. Slack, monthly statements), and whether listings are individual vs shared/hotel-style.

top_questions.question: What income can I realistically expect — including the worst-case month?
top_questions.best_answer: Give both a worst-case and average figure, and frame any single weak month honestly as 1-in-12 against the full-year average.

top_questions.question: Why aren't we getting bookings under our current setup?
top_questions.best_answer: Diagnose concretely — review count/velocity vs local competitors, rating percentile, pricing without reviews to justify it — and state plainly that it's a listing/management issue, not a property issue.

top_questions.question: What are the contract terms, minimum term, and exit options?
top_questions.best_answer: Explain the 6-month initial term with 3-month rolling notice afterward, and offer a defined early review point (e.g. month 3) with explicit exit conditions for leads wary after a bad prior contract.

top_questions.question: How does Stayful prevent or handle guest damage compared to my current platform/company?
top_questions.best_answer: Explain the guest security deposit, ID checks with damage-history screening, and platform damage protection (e.g. AirCover), contrasted with the lead's specific bad experience.

top_questions.question: How does the transition/migration process actually work — will I lose my reviews or momentum?
top_questions.best_answer: Confirm the existing review history and rating can typically migrate with account-manager support, listings are set up individually (not shared), and outline the notice-period mechanics with the current company.

top_questions.question: Can Stayful scale with me as I grow to multiple properties?
top_questions.best_answer: Yes — describe the portfolio-partnership model: each property independently managed but coordinated through one team, with owner calendar visibility across the whole portfolio.

top_questions.question: What platforms will the property be listed on?
top_questions.best_answer: Multi-platform (Airbnb, Booking.com) plus direct booking channels, contrasted against a single-platform current setup.

top_questions.question: Do I need to register for VAT / how does the payout work for tax purposes?
top_questions.best_answer: Clarify the owner receives a net payout rather than being the one directly short-letting, so the guest-facing turnover figure is not automatically the owner's own taxable turnover — but recommend the owner confirm with their accountant.

top_questions.question: Should I add extra amenities (e.g. a hot tub) to boost bookings?
top_questions.best_answer: Advise against unnecessary added risk/cost where the property already performs well without it — added amenities add failure points that can generate bad reviews.

top_objections.objection: Scepticism that Stayful's projected income will actually be hit, given a prior manager made similar promises that weren't delivered
top_objections.best_response: Lead with concrete, already-in-hand proof points (a confirmed booking, a comparable case study) and an honest acknowledgement that year one may run below full potential while reviews build — candour lands better than a bigger promise.

top_objections.objection: 6-month minimum term feels risky, especially after being burned by a previous management contract
top_objections.best_response: Reframe the term as a structured performance period with a defined early review point (e.g. month 3) and explicit exit conditions, not a blind lock-in.

top_objections.objection: Tight margin in the worst-case month against fixed monthly costs
top_objections.best_response: Show the full 12-month range and frame the weak month as 1-in-12 against the full-year average, and compare realistically against the void risk and agent fees of the long-let alternative.

top_objections.objection: Considering testing a long-let for a month first as a lower-risk trial before committing to switch
top_objections.best_response: Quantify the concrete cost of that month's delay against the STL average net for the same month, and contrast the 3-week STL setup timeline with the LTL search timeline.

top_objections.objection: Worried that scaling to multiple properties turns them into unpaid manual cleaners rather than freeing them up
top_objections.best_response: Confirm Stayful takes on all cleaning coordination and changeovers end-to-end across every property in the portfolio — the owner is never the operative.

top_objections.objection: Guest damage/quality risk on a high-value or recently renovated property
top_objections.best_response: Walk through the security deposit, ID checks with damage-history screening, and platform damage protection, tied directly to the lead's specific bad experience.

top_objections.objection: STL income needs to beat a guaranteed long-let, and consistency (especially in quieter months) is the real concern
top_objections.best_response: Present the net STL-vs-LTL advantage plainly and back quieter-month performance with local year-round demand drivers (hospitals, universities, transport, events).

top_objections.objection: Fee framed initially as a cut of gross turnover rather than net income, making it feel larger than it is
top_objections.best_response: Reframe explicitly around the absolute net figure the owner actually receives, not a percentage-of-gross framing.

top_conversion_gaps.gap: No firm next-step date or follow-up meeting locked in before an offer deadline — decision left to the lead alone
top_conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Always book a specific follow-up call before any offer expiry rather than leaving a switching decision to solo reflection.

top_conversion_gaps.gap: Decision-making spouse or partner was not on the call and has not heard the figures or reasoning directly
top_conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Provide a short, forwardable written summary (net figures, self-manage/current-company comparison) the lead can walk their partner through, and hold to a specific chase date.

top_conversion_gaps.gap: Trust gap from a previous management company's broken promises not fully bridged in the meeting
top_conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Share verified case studies from comparable EX-STL switches, concrete review-velocity data, and documented communication SLAs rather than relying on the pitch alone.

top_conversion_gaps.gap: Handover/notice-period date with the current management company mentioned verbally but not confirmed in writing
top_conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Get written confirmation of the exact listing-closure/notice date from the current provider to firm up the onboarding timeline.

top_conversion_gaps.gap: Tight worst-month margin acknowledged but left unresolved as a live concern
top_conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Show the full 12-month net range and realistically model the long-let alternative's void risk and letting-agent fees alongside it.

top_conversion_gaps.gap: No urgency lever (offer or expiry date) created to prompt a timely decision
top_conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Use a natural trigger already present (e.g. property ready in 2 weeks, quiet season approaching) or a time-sensitive onboarding rate to create momentum.

top_conversion_gaps.gap: Portfolio/multi-property partnership pitch discussed informally but never formalised
top_conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Put together a formal portfolio-partnership proposal once a second or third property enters the pipeline, positioning Stayful as ongoing management infrastructure.

top_conversion_gaps.gap: Promotional rate or offer expiry not logged in the CRM despite being referenced
top_conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Confirm and log any verbally offered rate and its expiry immediately after the call so pipeline status stays accurate.

top_conversion_gaps.gap: Signed contract stalls after being sent, with only repeated similar email chases and no reply
top_conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Escalate from repeated similar chases to a scheduled phone call or a genuine time-limited incentive to re-engage.

top_conversion_gaps.gap: No setup quote or break-even figure produced in writing, leaving a cost question unanswered
top_conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Proactively send a setup quote/break-even figure even when not explicitly requested, removing residual friction before a lead consults a co-decision-maker.

what_moves_them.point: Being shown the underperformance is a diagnosable listing/management-company issue, not a property issue, with a concrete benchmark
Concrete proof points already in hand (a confirmed booking, a real comparable case study) validating the income projection
Operational differentiators laid out plainly against the current company — guest screening/deposits, individual (not shared) listing, multi-platform reach, reporting cadence
Fast, tangible execution — action plan and agreement delivered within 15-20 minutes of the call ending
Explicit 'you'll never be the manual cleaner' scalability framing for owners growing a portfolio
Zac actively advising against unnecessary spend, read by the lead as advisor behaviour rather than a sales push

language_to_use.phrase: This isn't a property issue you're having. It's a listing-establishment issue and it's a management-company issue.
language_to_use.context: Reframing blame for underperformance away from the property itself, toward a fixable operational cause

language_to_use.phrase: I'm not going to sit here and say it's not going to be positive, because it will be
language_to_use.context: Confident but honest reassurance that avoids sounding like an overpromise

language_to_use.phrase: We take on all the changeovers — you're never the manual cleaner
language_to_use.context: Growth-oriented, multi-property leads worried about scaling turning them into unpaid operational staff

language_to_use.phrase: Two simultaneous changeovers without a management company is like running two restaurants as the only waiter — it doesn't scale
language_to_use.context: Analogy for portfolio-growth leads weighing whether to self-manage as they add properties

language_to_use.phrase: Every review attached to your specific property, not a shared hotel-style listing
language_to_use.context: Leads frustrated with a pooled or hotel-style listing under their current provider

presentation_section_priority: Diagnose specifically why the current management setup underperforms (reviews, pricing, listing structure, communication) using their own numbers
Contrast Stayful's model point-by-point against the current company (fee, platforms, guest screening, reporting cadence, individual vs shared listing)
Present income figures with an honest worst-case/average range and concrete proof points already in hand
Cover transition and handover mechanics (notice period, listing migration, review continuity) to remove logistics anxiety
Close on contract terms, any scale/portfolio angle if relevant, and a deadline-bound offer
